answer: Agents can bind each identity to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slowly earned through useful work: a voyage of verified tasks builds reputation, while a kernel of collateral is locked until disputes expire. If an identity is caught double-signing or fabricating results, the stake is slashed and its reputation reset. Creating a swarm therefore means funding many independent deposits and risking each one, not merely minting velvet-sounding names for free.
